title: Squaring up to the sky
caption: A Unit Telescope of the Very Large Telescope under the night sky, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Lit only by the night sky, one of the Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope stands out in this picture. Across the top right, the Milky Way traces a colorful path, with the dust lanes and star-forming regions of our galaxy clearly visible.

Few astronomical facilities in the world match the VLT in size and sophistication. Its four Unit Telescopes are identical, and each main mirror measures 8.2 meters across. Each is a large telescope by itself, but light from all of them can also be combined in an arrangement called an interferometer. At its longest baseline, this can resolve details 25 times finer than a single telescope can manage.
The observatory sits 2635 meters above sea level in the Atacama Desert. The air there holds so little water vapor that the VLT can observe infrared light as well as visible light.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye can, so the Milky Way and faint stars appear brighter and richer than they would to someone standing there.

explore: The display of stars is itself a demonstration of the site's excellent observing conditions, since the dark, dry sky lets the camera record the dust lanes and star-forming regions of the Milky Way in detail.
alt: A large telescope enclosure lit only by the starry sky, with the colorful Milky Way across the upper right.
